facts.statement: Juravenator lived approximately 152 to 151 million years ago in the Late Jurassic period in the Franconian Jura of Germany.
facts.quote: Juravenator is a genus of tetanuran theropod dinosaur which lived about 152 or 151 million years ago in modern day Franconian Jura of Germany (Torleite Formation) during the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Juravenator is a juvenile individual measuring about 75 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: It is known from a single, juvenile specimen measuring about 75 cm in length.

facts.statement: Juravenator was a small bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Juravenator was a small bipedal predator.

facts.statement: The four front teeth of the premaxilla had serrations on the upper third of their back edges.
facts.quote: The four teeth of the premaxilla in the front of the snout had serrations on the upper third of the back edge of the tooth crown.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen possessed eight maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: The maxillary teeth were few in number, eight with the holotype.

facts.statement: The zygapophyses in the middle of the tail were bow-shaped.
facts.quote: The zygapophyses in the middle of the tail were bow-shaped.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered during a 1998 paleontological expedition organized by the Jura-Museum Eichstätt at the Schamhaupten chalk quarry.
facts.quote: In the summer of 1998, the Jura-Museum Eichstätt at Eichstätt organised a paleontological expedition to the nearby chalk quarry of Schamhaupten.

facts.statement: Juravenator starki was formally named and described in 2006 by Ursula Göhlich and Luis Chiappe.
facts.quote: In 2006 the type species Juravenator starki was named and described by Ursula Göhlich and Luis Chiappe.

facts.statement: Small areas of the fossil preserve impressions or remains of soft tissues.
facts.quote: In small areas impressions or remains of the soft parts are present.

facts.statement: Fossilized skin from the tail and lower hind leg shows normal dinosaur scales alongside traces of what may be simple feathers.
facts.quote: A patch of fossilized Juravenator skin (from the tail, between the eighth and twenty-second vertebra, and lower hind leg) shows primarily normal dinosaur scales, as well as traces of what may be simple feathers.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Juravenator may have been nocturnal, though this might be due to the specimen being a juvenile.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Juravenator and modern birds and reptiles indicate that it may have been nocturnal.

facts.statement: Researchers interpreted small round structures on the tail as integumentary sense organs similar to those of crocodiles, which would be the first such organs found in dinosaur skin.
facts.quote: They interpreted these as "integumentary sense organs" like those on the scales of crocodiles. If this identification is correct, these would be the first sensory organs found in the skin of any dinosaur.

facts.statement: Juravenator may have used these sensory organs to detect aquatic prey like fish while wading in water.
facts.quote: Juravenator may have used these to detect the movement of aquatic prey, such as fish, as it waded in the water.

facts.statement: Some studies classify Juravenator as a basal member of Maniraptora rather than a compsognathid.
facts.quote: Rather than grouping it with Sinosauropteryx and other compsognathids, Butler et al. found that it was not a compsognathid, but rather a basal member of the group Maniraptora.

facts.statement: A 2013 analysis classified Juravenator as a coelurosaur closely related to but not part of Compsognathidae, placing it near Ornitholestes outside Maniraptoriformes.
facts.quote: In 2013 again found Juravenator to be a coelurosaur closely related to, but not a member of, the Compsognathidae. Instead, it was recovered as a close relative of Ornitholestes outside the clade Maniraptoriformes.

facts.statement: A 2020 study suggested Juravenator might be a non-coelurosaurian tetanuran belonging to the megalosauroid group.
facts.quote: Foth et al. (2020) considered it plausible that Juravenator may have been a non-coelurosaurian tetanuran, potentially part of the megalosauroid group along with the similar Sciurumimus.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding whether compsognathids belong within Maniraptora or represent a more primitive group.
facts.quote: Studies conflict on whether or not compsognathids belong to this later group or are more primitive.

facts.statement: Juravenator lived in what is now Germany during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en las Montañas de Jura en Alemania.

facts.statement: Juravenator lived approximately 150 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 150 millones de años, durante el Kimmeridgiense

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Juravenator represents a juvenile individual measuring about 75 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El holotipo representa un individuo juvenil, de unos 75 centímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest that Juravenator may have been nocturnal.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos esclerales de Juravenator y las aves y reptiles modernos indican que puede haber sido nocturno.

facts.statement: Juravenator was originally classified as a member of the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Juravenator se clasificó originalmente como un miembro de Compsognathidae

facts.statement: A fossilized skin patch from Juravenator's tail shows mostly normal dinosaur scales alongside traces of what may be simple feathers.
facts.quote: un parche de piel fosilizada de Juravenator, desde la cola, entre la vértebra octava y vigésima segunda y la pata trasera inferior, muestra escamas de dinosaurios principalmente normales, así como rastros de lo que pueden ser plumas simples.

facts.statement: UV examination revealed extensive filamentous structures on Juravenator similar in anatomy to primitive feathers found in other compsognathids like Sinosauropteryx.
facts.quote: El examen bajo UV reveló una cobertura más extensa de estructuras similares a filamentos, similar en anatomía a las plumas primitivas de otros compsognátidos, incluido Sinosauropteryx.

facts.statement: The Juravenator specimen was found in almost complete articulation, with only the skull, pelvic girdle, and front tail section partially disarticulated.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in almost in full articulation (bones still connected together), only the skull, pelvic girdle, and front section of the tail were disarticulated to some degree.

facts.statement: Small rounded stones interpreted as ooids were found within the belly area of the Juravenator specimen.
facts.quote: Reisdorf and Wuttke, in 2012, discovered small, rounded stones within the belly area that they interpreted as ooids.

facts.statement: Fossils of isopods found with the specimen suggest they scavenged the carcass while it was floating.
facts.quote: Chiappe and Göhlich identified fossils of isopods found with the specimen, and concluded that these animals likely have scavenged the carcass while it was still floating.

facts.statement: Researchers debated whether the isopods found with Juravenator scavenged the carcass or parasitized the living animal.
facts.quote: Reisdorf and Wuttke, in 2012, stated that the isopods could alternatively have parasitising the living animal.

facts.statement: The genus Juravenator was named by Göhlich and Chiappe in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Göhlich & Chiappe, 2006

facts.statement: The species Juravenator starki was named by Göhlich and Chiappe in 2006.
facts.quote: species_authority: Göhlich & Chiappe, 2006

facts.statement: In the summer of 1998, a paleontological expedition was organized by the Jura-Museum Eichstätt at the nearby Schamhaupten chalk quarry.
facts.quote: En el verano de 1998, el Jura-Museum Eichstätt en Eichstätt organizó una expedición paleontológica a la cercana cantera de tiza de Schamhaupten.

facts.statement: Near the end of planned excavations, two volunteers, Klaus-Dieter Weiß and his brother Hans-Joachim Weiß, found a chalk slab showing clear remains of vertebrates.
facts.quote: Cerca del final de las excavaciones planificadas, dos voluntarios, Klaus-Dieter Weiß y su hermano Hans-Joachim Weiß, encontraron una placa de tiza en la que se veían restos claros de vertebrados.

facts.statement: Initial preparation revealed the head of a small theropod.
facts.quote: Una primera preparación descubrió la cabeza de un pequeño terópodo.

facts.statement: The find was reported in scientific literature in 1999 by Günther Viohl.
facts.quote: En 1999, el hallazgo fue reportado en la literatura científica por Günther Viohl.

facts.statement: In 2001, the fossil gained publicity and was nicknamed "Borsti" in German press, assuming the creature had protofeathers like bristles.
facts.quote: En 2001, el fósil había generado algo de publicidad y fue apodado "Borsti" en la prensa alemana, un nombre comúnmente dado a los perros con pelo de cerdas, bajo el supuesto de que la criatura estaba dotada de protoplumas como cerdas.

facts.statement: In 2003, new museum director Martina Kölbl-Ebert decided to complete the preparation.
facts.quote: En 2003, la nueva directora del museo, Martina Kölbl-Ebert, decidió terminar la preparación.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Jura Mountains and the Latin word venator meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del nombre de las montañas del Jura y el vocablo latino venator por "cazador".

facts.statement: The specific name honors the Stark family, owners of the quarry.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a la familia Stark, propietarios de la cantera.

facts.statement: The holotype, JME Sch 200, was found in the Malm Epsilon 2 layer of the Painten formation, dating to the Kimmeridgian, about 151 to 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo , JME Sch 200, se encontró en el Malm Epsilon 2 , una capa de marga de la formación Painten que data del Kimmeridgiense, hace unos 151 a 152 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of an articulated nearly complete skeleton with the skull of a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: El fósil consiste en un esqueleto articulado casi completo con el cráneo de un individuo juvenil.

facts.statement: The fossil was considered the most complete non-avian theropod specimen ever found in Europe.
facts.quote: El fósil fue considerado el espécimen más completo de un terópodo no aviar jamás encontrado en Europa.

facts.statement: Small areas show impressions or remains of soft tissues.
facts.quote: En áreas pequeñas hay impresiones o restos de las partes blandas.

facts.statement: Although first classified as a member of Compsognathidae, later studies found problems with the initial study that produced those findings.
facts.quote: Si bien se clasificó por primera vez como miembro de Compsognathidae, los estudios posteriores han encontrado problemas con el estudio inicial que produjo esos hallazgos.

facts.statement: Instead of grouping it with Sinosauropteryx and other compsognathids, Butler et al. found it was a basal member of the Maniraptora group.
facts.quote: En lugar de agruparlo con Sinosauropteryx y otros compsognátidos, Butler et al. descubrió que era un miembro basal del grupo Maniraptora.

facts.statement: Additional work published by Luis Chiappe and Ursula Göhlich in 2010 found Juravenator was anatomically similar to Compsognathus and likely belonged to Compsognathidae if that is a natural group.
facts.quote: El trabajo adicional publicado por Luis Chiappe y Ursula Göhlich en 2010 encontró que Juravenator era más similar en anatomía a Compsognathus, y que probablemente pertenecía a Compsognathidae si ese es realmente un grupo natural.

facts.statement: In 2011, Cristiano dal Sasso and Simone Maganuco published an analysis recovering Compsognathidae as a natural group and Juravenator as a sister species to Sinosauropteryx.
facts.quote: En 2011, Cristiano dal Sasso y Simone Maganuco publicaron un análisis que recuperó a los Compsognathidae como un grupo natural y a Juravenator como una especie hermana de Sinosauropteryx.

facts.statement: However, a large coelurosaur analysis published in 2013 again found Juravenator as a coelurosaur closely related to, but not a member of, Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un gran análisis de celurosaurios publicado en 2013 nuevamente encontró a Juravenator como un celurosaurio estrechamente relacionado con, pero no miembro de, el Compsognathidae.

facts.statement: Instead, it was recovered as a close relative of Ornitholestes outside the Maniraptoriformes clade.
facts.quote: En cambio, se recuperó como un pariente cercano de Ornitholestes fuera del clado Maniraptoriformes.

facts.statement: Juravenator lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, from 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Juravenator belongs to the parent group Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coelurosauria

facts.statement: Juravenator is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
